captions.detailed: A traditional Japanese temple bell pavilion (shōrō) featuring a dark-brown open timber frame on four corner posts with grey stone bases. Hanging from the center of the main cross-beam yoke is a large, dark metallic bonshō bell, which can pivot via a revolute joint. Suspended horizontally alongside the bell is a wooden striker log, supported by two vertical arms on revolute pins to allow a pendulum swinging motion for striking.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a Japanese temple bell pavilion. The model must feature a square wooden support frame with four corner posts on stone bases, a curved dark roof, a central hanging cast-iron bonshō bell, and a horizontal wooden striker log suspended on swing arms. Ensure both the bell and the striker log have revolute joints to simulate realistic movement.
captions.factory: Construct the main pavilion base using box primitives for the wooden posts, horizontal beams, and grey base stones. Model the curved roof using a lofted or swept profile capped with a small decorative top cylinder. Define the bonshō bell by revolving a custom 2D profile to form its characteristic tapered shape. Create the striker log assembly using cylinders for the main log and rectangular prisms for the vertical hanger arms, then define revolute articulations for both the bell pivot and the striker swing arms.
